ai.description: *Raorchestes signatus* is a small bush frog (2–3 cm) with a distinct dark, cross-shaped marking on its back. It features a pale green or yellowish body with prominent red-orange toe pads.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Raorchestes signatus* is best distinguished by the distinct, dark "X" or hourglass-shaped marking on its dorsum, which is absent in most other similar bush frogs.
ai.habitat: *Raorchestes signatus* inhabits high-altitude evergreen forests and shola grasslands in the Western Ghats, typically found at elevations between 1,500 and 2,500 meters.
ai.behavior: The Cross-backed Bush Frog is primarily nocturnal, emerging at night to forage for small invertebrates among the foliage of its high-altitude forest habitat.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Raorchestes signatus* exhibits direct development, bypassing the tadpole stage. They lay small clutches of terrestrial eggs, typically breeding during the monsoon season.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Raorchestes signatus* is endemic to the high-altitude shola forests and grasslands of the southern Western Ghats in Kerala and Tamil Nadu, above 1,500 meters.
ai.callDescription: The advertisement call of *Raorchestes signatus* consists of a series of high-pitched, insect-like chirps, typically heard from vegetation in high-altitude shola forests.
